final_query:
MATCH (p:Person)-[:PERFORMS_VISIT]->(v:Visit)
WITH p.healthstatus AS healthStatus, p.id AS personId,
     count(v) AS visitCount,
     sum(v.duration.days * 86400 + v.duration.hours * 3600 + v.duration.minutes * 60 + v.duration.seconds) AS totalDurationSeconds
RETURN healthStatus, avg(visitCount) AS avgVisitCount,
       toFloat(sum(totalDurationSeconds)) / sum(visitCount) AS avgVisitDurationSeconds

critique.feedback: The entity model is correct: (:Person)-[:PERFORMS_VISIT]->(:Visit), with Visit.duration as the owner of the duration value and Person.healthstatus as the grouping key; counting v in the first WITH is also the right basis for the average number of visits performed per person. The mismatch is in the visit-duration measure. Because the first WITH groups by (healthStatus, personId), each row is one person, and avg(duration.inSeconds(v.duration)) is only that person's mean. The final RETURN's avg(avgDurationPerVisit) is therefore an unweighted average of per-person means, which answers 'average of each person's average visit duration', not the question's 'average duration of those visits'. It equals the true value only if every person in the group has the same number of visits; a person with 1 long visit counts as much as a person with 10 short ones. Fix: in the first WITH, keep count(v) AS visitCount and replace the per-person avg with sum(duration.inSeconds(v.duration)) AS totalDurationSeconds (v.duration is valid because v is the Visit reached via PERFORMS_VISIT). In the final RETURN, keep avg(visitCount) AS avgVisitCount and replace avg(avgDurationPerVisit) with sum(totalDurationSeconds) / sum(visitCount) AS avgVisitDurationSeconds. The final grouping by healthStatus alone is already correct once personId is no longer carried forward. Secondary, interpretation-dependent: the inner MATCH drops persons with zero visits, so they are excluded from avgVisitCount. Include them only if the question should treat those persons as having 0 visits.
